candidates.statement: Equation (1) is usually called the braid equation. An operator R satisﬁes (1) if and only if R ◦T satisﬁes the quantum Yang–Baxter equation R12 ◦R13 ◦R23 = R23 ◦R13 ◦R12. Given a (unitary associative) k–algebra A and scalars x, y, z ∈k, we consider the k–linear map Rx,y,z : A ⊗A →A ⊗A deﬁned by Rx,y,z(a ⊗b) = x · ab ⊗1 + y · 1 ⊗ab −z · a ⊗b for any a, b ∈A. The following theorem determines the situations where this map is a Yang–Baxter operator.
candidates.section_title: Yang--Baxter operators arising from algebra structures

candidates.name: D˘asc˘alescu–Nichita [1]
candidates.statement: Let A be a k–algebra of dimension at least 2 and let x, y, z ∈k be scalars. Then Rx,y,z is a Yang–Baxter operator if and only if one of the following conditions holds: (i) x = z̸ = 0, y̸ = 0, (ii) y = z̸ = 0, x̸ = 0, (iii) x = y = 0, z̸ = 0. If so, its inverse is given by Rx,y,z−1 = Ry−1,x−1,z−1 in cases (i) and (ii), and by R0,0,z−1 = R0,0,z−1 in case (iii). We will be only interested in the non–trivial cases (i) and (ii) (which are equivalent through inversion) and we will denote by Rx,y the operator Rx,y,x. Observe that (2) Rx,y −xy · Rx,y−1 = (y −x) · Id⊗2 and that, in particular, the minimal polynomial of Rx,y is of degree 2. Next result

candidates.name: D˘asc˘alescu–Nichita [1]
candidates.statement: Let A and A′ be k–algebras of dimension at least 2, and let x, y, x′, y′ be nonzero scalars. Then the YB operators Rx,y and Rx′,y′ associated to A and A′ respectively are isomorphic if, and only if, x = x′, y = y′ and the k–algebras A and A′ are isomorphic.

candidates.statement: In fact, according to the proof of [1, Proposition 3.1], a bijective k–linear map f : A →A′ is such that Rx′,y′ ◦(f ⊗f) = (f ⊗f) ◦Rx,y if and only if x = x′, y = y′ and f is, up to multiplication by a scalar, an isomorphism of k–algebras. (Note that the assumption char(k)̸ = 2 is used here.)

candidates.name: Turaev [12]
candidates.statement: Let S be an enhanced YB operator. If two braids b1 and b2 have isotopic closures, then their Markov traces TS(b1) and TS(b2) are equal. So, there is an isotopy invariant XS of oriented links deﬁned by XS  bb  = TS(b).

candidates.statement: Let S be a redundant YB operator. If two braids b1 and b2 have isotopic closures, then their modiﬁed Markov traces TS,1(b1) and TS,1(b2) are equal. So, there is an isotopy invariant XS,1 of oriented links deﬁned by XS,1  bb  = TS,1(b).

candidates.statement: If S = (R, µ, α, β) is a redundant Yang–Baxter operator, then we have that XS (L) = Trace(µ) · XS,1(L) for any oriented link L. In particular, if Trace(µ) vanishes, then XS does too: this is the case when it is worth working with modiﬁed Markov traces. Next proposition will be proved thanks to arguments from [8, Appendix A]. There, Murakami shows redundancy of a particular (colored) enhanced Yang–Baxter operator, from which he derives the (multivariable) Alexander polynomial.
